A researcher reported a zero-click, wormable RCE chain in MS Teams; Microsoft rated it only 'Important/Spoofing' and marked the desktop client RCE 'out of scope', drawing criticism for how low the severity rating was given 115M daily users.
User: 'So glad Microsoft installed teams on our server with an update even though we never asked for it.'
'I refuse to install this junk, it's Google Meet or bust for us... For now Google seems to have their act together on this,' citing repeated vulnerabilities in Teams.

'We use zoom but are switching to teams... To my horror it was the epitome of bloat. It essentially takes a screenshot of the presenters desktop and then starts a whiteboard session. It takes a good 30 seconds to enable' - describing Teams' 'active annotation' feature as poorly implemented.
'Teams is buggy, clunky, and unreliable, though fairly feature rich. I find things like Google stuff/Slack/Discord to be somewhat more reliable and less unpleasant to use.'
'Absolutely incredibly garbage... I experienced a situation where everyone could see and hear only about half of the other meeting participants, but not the same set for everyone.'
Suggestion from a user: install Teams as a web app via Edge instead of the Electron desktop client, since 'the web app version... is faster and more stable.'

Detailed complaint: search is abysmal, messages go missing in 1:1 chats, images fail to display, notifications get lost, and the app window sometimes disappears after waking a Mac, requiring relaunch.

Complaint list: no ability to link to conversations, inconsistent UI between channels and direct chats (no threading/code blocks in DMs), notifications in channels easy to miss, poor emoji customization, and annotation mode gets 'stuck'.
'I've had many critical bugs, including the video on/off & audio mute button failing during calls, the join call UI being broken/missing, join links being broken.'

Long complaint list: can't filter Files by type or search within a channel, search results can't be sorted except by date modified, T-Bot chat entry is greyed out and unusable, and API integration requires the full Azure/Graph API stack unlike Slack's simple webhooks.
'Teams is horribly unintuitive to use. The UI is much worse than Slack. Took me long to realise I was looking at the chat window and to follow along the threads.'
'you can't seem to attach a .json file... though renaming it to .json.txt works... the automatic conversion of things like ;) to animated emoji... please give me an option to turn this off.'

'MS have not implemented muting as a feature... you can't unsubscribe yourself... Unavoidable alerts that any idiot on any channel can annoy people with.' At my last job we figured out the fastest way to get your company off Teams: add the CEO to a chatty channel.

'My biggest grief with Teams is that it's impossible to shut off notifications. With pretty much everything turned off... it still blinks the icon and shows number of unread notifications in the taskbar.'
Positive take: 'we use it as a file share and central information home... it is far better than sharing a bunch of files in email threads or maintaining unofficial google docs.'
'My team hated it, I tolerated it... The biggest issue was the threading; it truly beggars belief... Moving (and paying) for Slack was the best decision I made.'

'Teams is blocking Firefox Nightly'—users found teams.live.com showed 'unsupported browser' errors for Firefox (stable, ESR, Nightly) and even Safari mobile, while teams.microsoft.com worked fine, suggesting sloppy user-agent detection rather than a deliberate block.

'This is not just nightly, even Firefox-esr on Debian didn't support screen-sharing at least a few months ago... It's not technical it's lazy devs. The button is disabled claiming my browser doesn't support it.'
'I can't use same sso account on android and on macos at the same time. The token gets invalidated for some reason.'
